who: Canadian legal historian at the University of Toronto, PhD in history, Dalhousie University, 1983.

evidence.says: Identifies Jim Phillips as Toronto law faculty cross-appointed to History; records his Dalhousie history PhD in 1983. Its 1994 source already places him at Toronto.

Phillips's 2010 article identifies his Toronto Law and History appointments. On page 311 he discusses his current doctoral student's extradition research; footnote 62 identifies Bradley Miller and the forthcoming Emptying the Den of Thieves dissertation.
This other Jim Phillips lists University of Glasgow employment and works on Scottish coal miners and deindustrialization.
This other authority identifies the author of The Great Alliance and Cheated Not Poisoned?, a lecturer in Economic and Social History at Glasgow.

notes: The Toronto authority matches both the doctorate and the named student. The Glasgow ORCID candidate p-16673 and LC candidate p-113695 concern a different historian.

who: Harold L. Platt, urban historian at Loyola University Chicago, PhD Rice University, 1974.

evidence.says: Loyola's archival biography records a Rice PhD in 1974 and Loyola History employment from 1974, including professor from 1990 to 2012; research concerns urban history and public utilities.
Identifies Harold L. Platt as Loyola history professor emeritus with a Rice PhD in 1974; names City Building in the New South and Sinking Chicago among his works.

notes: Exact doctoral institution and year agree; the documented Loyola appointment covers Blanke's 1996 dissertation.

who: Peter Edward Pope, historian and archaeologist at Memorial University of Newfoundland, history PhD Memorial, 1992.

evidence.says: Memorial records Pope's history PhD there in 1992, his academic career there beginning in 1988, and appointments in history, anthropology and archaeology.
Identifies Peter Edward Pope, also using Peter Pope and Peter E. Pope, as Memorial's archaeology research professor cross-appointed to History in a 2013 university source.
Memorial's fall 2014 convocation programme names Peter Pope as Christopher Patrick Aylward's supervisor for The Beothuk Story.

notes: Authority, doctorate and direct supervision record agree. The convocation programme places Aylward's degree in Interdisciplinary Studies.

who: John Price, historian of modern Japan and transpacific relations at the University of Victoria, PhD University of British Columbia.

evidence.says: Victoria's History profile lists Price as emeritus professor and adjunct, with BA, MA and PhD from UBC, specializing in modern Japan and transpacific history.
Identifies John Price as Victoria history professor researching Canada-East Asian relations; an earlier source places him at UBC's Institute of Asian Research.
Simon Nantais's Koreans and the Politics of Nationality and Race dissertation names John Price of the History Department as supervisor.

notes: The LC identity, university profile and named student's thesis agree. The profile confirms the doctoral institution but does not state the PhD year.

who: Lowell Joseph Ragatz, historian of the Caribbean and European expansion, chiefly at Ohio State University, PhD Wisconsin, 1925.

evidence.says: The Wisconsin alumni exhibit identifies Lowell Ragatz as BA 1920, MA 1921 and PhD 1925, and describes his history career, chiefly at Ohio State.
Connects Lowell J. Ragatz, Lowell Joseph Ragatz and Lowell Ragatz; cites The Old Plantation System and an Ohio State affiliation.
A contemporary departmental report states that Lowell Ragatz, Ohio State's history chairman, taught a summer session at the University of Southern California in 1951.

notes: Name, exact Wisconsin doctorate year and field support the identity match, with a documented earlier USC teaching connection. Supervision of Rogers's 1970 USC dissertation was not independently confirmed; the 1951 appointment does not establish a 1970 USC position.

who: Bradly Ward Reed, historian of late imperial and modern China at the University of Virginia, PhD UCLA, 1994.

evidence.says: Virginia's History profile identifies Bradly W. Reed, lists a UCLA PhD in 1994, and describes his specializations in late imperial and modern China, law, society and local administration.
The authority for Bradly Ward Reed cites Scoundrels and Civil Servants, 1994, whose title page identifies him as receiving a PhD in History at UCLA.

notes: Distinctive name, exact doctorate institution and year, Virginia affiliation and Chinese history field agree. Yang's individual supervision was not independently confirmed.

who: Bryan C. Rindfleisch, historian of early America and Native American history at Marquette University, PhD Oklahoma, 2014 according to his CV.

evidence.says: Bryan C. Rindfleisch's university-hosted CV lists a history PhD from Oklahoma in 2014 and Marquette history appointments from 2015 onward; names George Galphin's Intimate Empire among his books.
Identifies Bryan C. Rindfleisch as the author of George Galphin's Intimate Empire, with a PhD in Native American History from Oklahoma and an MA from Marquette.
Marquette's repository names Bryan Rindfleisch as first advisor of Timothy Lee Houge's spring 2025 History PhD dissertation on Indigenous-sovereign educational activism, 1960–1975.

notes: Direct supervision and the authority's works and education establish the match. The CV gives 2014, rather than the AHA's 2015, for his doctorate. Houge's final repository title differs from the AHA title.

who: Fritz K. Ringer, historian of German and European intellectual and social history at Pittsburgh, PhD Harvard, 1961.

evidence.says: The AHA obituary identifies Fritz K. Ringer as Pittsburgh history professor emeritus, records his Harvard PhD in 1961 and retirement from Pittsburgh in 2002, and describes his German and European intellectual history scholarship.
Pittsburgh's graduate alumni directory pairs Leslie Hammond with advisor Fritz Ringer for The British Progressive Contribution to the League of Nations Ideal, 2001.
The authority heading is Ringer, Fritz K.; its source citations identify the author of Die Gelehrten.

notes: Direct supervision, Pittsburgh career and exact Harvard doctorate year agree with the candidate's Fritz K. Ringer identity.
